newsitem.title: UK: LME copper finishes weaker, wipes out big gains.
newsitem.headline: LME copper finishes weaker, wipes out big gains.

text.p: Copper prices finished lower on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Monday despite surging to a 2-1/2 month high early on.

Three month futures ended the afternoon kerb close at $2,026 a tonne, down $13 from Friday's afternoon close but some $139 below the highs hit in inter-office trade on the pre-market. The low of $2,016 was hit just before the finish.

Persistent selling of cash and three months copper, forward selling and nearby spread lending eroded the gains. Expectations of a build in stocks when the next LME data is released early on Tuesday also knocked values lower.
Traders said the market surged early on options-related covering and fund short-covering on the futures market.
The fact that volumes were so thin early on the pre-market exaggerated the move, they added.
"The market was marked up in thin air during a huge frenzy early on," said Robin Bhar, analyst at Brandeis.
